lessons.title: a or an?
lessons.art_alt: Crumb the little baker dragon looks up at the bakery sign

hook.text: Oh no! Crumb the little baker dragon wrote a new bakery sign: “a apple pie”. Say it out loud. It sounds bumpy! Can you help Crumb fix it?
hook.say: Oh no! Crumb the little baker dragon wrote a new bakery sign: “a apple pie”. Say it out loud. It sounds bumpy! Can you help Crumb fix it?

discover.text: Which little word goes in front? Drag each treat into the a basket or the an basket.
discover.hint: Say it out loud: “an apple” slides smoothly, but “a apple” bumps.

items.why: Apple starts with a. Say “an apple”.
Cake starts with c. Say “a cake”.
Egg starts with e. Say “an egg”.
Cookie starts with c. Say “a cookie”.
Orange starts with o. Say “an orange”.
Banana starts with b. Say “a banana”.
Ice cream starts with i. Say “an ice cream”.
Bun starts with b. Say “a bun”.

discover.say: Which little word goes in front? Drag each treat into the a basket or the an basket.

rule.text: Use an before words that start with a, e, i, o or u. Use a before all the other letters.
examples: an apple · an egg · an ice cream
a cake · a cookie · a banana
rule.say: Use an before words that start with a, e, i, o or u. Use a before all the other letters.
sayEx: an apple , an egg , an ice cream
a cake , a cookie , a banana

notes.a: Egg starts with e, so we say an egg, not a egg.
notes.two: Two means more than one, so it would be two egg tarts. Here there is one tart.

check.explain: Egg starts with e, so it takes an: an egg tart.
check.say: Crumb bakes blank egg tart.

notes.an: Banana starts with b, not a, e, i, o or u, so we say a banana.
notes.some: Some is for lots of things. One banana takes a.

check.explain: Banana starts with b, so it takes a: a banana.
check.say: I have blank banana.

notes.a orange cake: Orange starts with o, so it takes an: an orange cake.
notes.an cake: Cake starts with c, so we say a cake. Here the word after an is orange.

check.explain: The word right after the little word decides. Orange starts with o, so: an orange cake.
check.say: Which sign is right?

reteach.text: Here's another way to check. Say both out loud and listen to your mouth. “a apple” makes your mouth stop and bump. “an apple” slides smoothly. The little n is a bridge to words that start with a, e, i, o or u!

discover.text: Try the bridge trick! Drag each word to a or an.
discover.hint: Does it start with a, e, i, o or u? Then it needs the n bridge: an.

items.why: Owl starts with o: an owl.
Dog starts with d: a dog.
Umbrella starts with u: an umbrella.
Hat starts with h: a hat.

discover.say: Try the bridge trick! Drag each word to a or an.

reteach.say: Here's another way to check. Say both out loud and listen to your mouth. “a apple” makes your mouth stop and bump. “an apple” slides smoothly. The little n is a bridge to words that start with a, e, i, o or u!

notes.A: Owl starts with o, so we need the n bridge: An owl!
notes.Two: Two means more than one, so it would be two owls. Here there is one owl.

check2.explain: Owl starts with o, so: An owl!

notes.a: Umbrella starts with u, so it takes an: an umbrella.
notes.some: Some is for lots of things. One umbrella takes an.

check2.explain: Umbrella starts with u, so: an umbrella.

notes.an dog: Dog starts with d, so no n bridge: a dog.
notes.a owl: Owl starts with o, so it needs an: an owl.

check2.explain: Dog starts with d, so: a dog.

lessons.grown: 👪 Indefinite articles a / an (Cambridge Pre-A1 Starters). Taught by first letter at A1; the 'vowel sound' refinement (an hour, a unicorn) comes at A2.

lessons.title: am, is, are
lessons.art_alt: Puffbun hands out name badges in the meadow

hook.text: It's Name Badge Day in the meadow! Puffbun wrote everyone's badge, but a little word is missing in each one. Can you finish them?
hook.say: It's Name Badge Day in the meadow! Puffbun wrote everyone's badge, but a little word is missing in each one. Can you finish them?

discover.text: Drag the right little word into the gap. You can also tap a word.
discover.hint: I always goes with am. One person or thing goes with is. You, we and they go with are.

items.why: With I we always say am: I am Puffbun.
She is one person, so we say is: She is Lily.
They is more than one, so we say are: They are friends.
It is one thing, so we say is: It is a frog.
With we we say are: We are happy.
With you we say are: You are kind.

discover.say: Drag the right little word into the gap. You can also tap a word.

rule.text: I goes with am. He, she and it go with is. You, we and they go with are.
examples: She is my friend. It is a frog.
We are happy. They are friends.
rule.say: I goes with am. He, she and it go with is. You, we and they go with are.
sayEx: She is my friend. It is a frog.
We are happy. They are friends.

check.q: Tom and Mia ___ in the garden.

notes.is: Tom and Mia are two people, like they, so we use are.

check.explain: Two people are like they, so: Tom and Mia are in the garden.
check.say: Tom and Mia blank in the garden.

notes.is: With I we always use am: I am seven.
notes.are: Are goes with you, we and they. With I, use am.

check.explain: I always goes with am: I am seven.
check.say: I blank seven.

notes.are: One cat is like it, so we use is.

check.explain: One cat is like it, so: The cat is sleepy.
check.say: The cat blank sleepy.

reteach.text: Here's another way. Swap the name for a little word first! Tom becomes he, so it's is. Tom and Mia become they, so it's are. Me becomes I, so it's am.
examples: Tom and Mia → they → They are tall.

discover.text: Swap and sort! Drag each word to am, is or are.
discover.hint: Swap it for I, he, she, it, we or they first.

items.why: I always takes am.
My dog is one, like it: is.
Sam is one person, like he: is.
We takes are.
The birds are more than one, like they: are.
You takes are.

discover.say: Swap and sort! Drag each word to am, is or are.

reteach.say: Here's another way. Swap the name for a little word first! Tom becomes he, so it's is. Tom and Mia become they, so it's are. Me becomes I, so it's am.

notes.are: My mum is one person, like she, so we use is.

check2.explain: My mum is like she, so: My mum is a teacher.

notes.is: We means more than one person, so we use are.
notes.am: Am only goes with I. We takes are.

check2.explain: We goes with are: We are at school.

notes.Is: Is goes with he, she and it. You takes are.
notes.Am: Am only goes with I. You takes are.

check2.explain: You goes with are, so the question is: Are you happy?

lessons.grown: 👪 The verb to be in the present: am / is / are (Pre-A1 Starters), via subject pronoun substitution.

lessons.title: One cat, two cats
lessons.art_alt: Hoot the owl counts animals in the meadow

hook.text: Hoot the owl is counting the animals for the picnic list. But the list looks funny: three cat, two dog… Something is missing at the end of the words!
hook.say: Hoot the owl is counting the animals for the picnic list. But the list looks funny: three cat, two dog… Something is missing at the end of the words!

discover.text: Drag the s stamp onto the words that need it. You can also tap a word to stamp it.
discover.hint: Look at the number. Only one? No s. Two or more? Add s!

items.why: Three is more than one: cats.
Just one frog, so no s!
Two is more than one: dogs.
Four is more than one: birds.
Just one bee, so no s!
Five is more than one: apples.

discover.say: Drag the s stamp onto the words that need it. You can also tap a word to stamp it.

rule.text: One thing: no s, like one cat. More than one: add s, like two cats and three dogs.
examples: A few special words change instead: one foot → two feet.
rule.say: One thing: no s, like one cat. More than one: add s, like two cats and three dogs.
sayEx: A few special words change instead: one foot, two feet.

notes.bird: Three is more than one, so add s: birds.
notes.a bird: A bird means one bird, but the sentence says three.

check.explain: Three is more than one, so: three birds.
check.say: I can see three blank.

check.q: There is one ___ on the bed.

notes.cats: One cat, so no s for just one.
notes.two cats: The sentence says one, not two.

check.explain: Just one, so no s: one cat.
check.say: There is one blank on the bed.

notes.four apple: Four is more than one, so it needs s: apples.
notes.a apples: A means one, so it can't go with apples. Say an apple, or four apples.

check.explain: Four is more than one, so: four apples.
check.say: Which is right?

reteach.text: Here's another way. Count on your fingers! One finger up? No s. Two or more fingers up? Add s, like a little snake going sss: cats, dogs, birds!

discover.text: Finger check! Stamp s only where there's more than one.
discover.hint: One finger? No s. Two or more? Stamp the s!

items.why: Two fingers up: hats.
One finger up: just one sun, no s.
Six is more than one: stars.
One finger up: just one ball, no s.

discover.say: Finger check! Stamp s only where there's more than one.

notes.a duck: A duck means one, but the sentence says two.

check2.explain: Two is more than one: two ducks.

notes.pencils: Just one, so no s: one pencil.
notes.two pencils: The sentence says one, not two.

check2.explain: Just one: one pencil.

notes.five cake: Five is more than one, so it needs s: cakes.
notes.a cakes: A means one, so say a cake, or five cakes.

check2.explain: Five is more than one: five cakes.

lessons.grown: 👪 Regular plural nouns with -s (Pre-A1 Starters). Irregular plurals (feet, mice, children) are only mentioned here; they get their own lesson later.

lessons.title: in, on, under
lessons.art_alt: Puffbun hides under the table while Lily counts

hook.text: Puffbun loves hide-and-seek! Lily is counting to ten. Can you hide Puffbun in the places the words say?
hook.say: Puffbun loves hide-and-seek! Lily is counting to ten. Can you hide Puffbun in the places the words say?

discover.text: Drag Puffbun to the right place. You can also tap the place.
discover.hint: On is on top. Under is below. In is inside.

tasks.say: Put Puffbun ON the table.

tasks.say: Now put Puffbun UNDER the table.

tasks.say: Now put Puffbun IN the basket.

discover.say: Drag Puffbun to the right place. You can also tap the place.

rule.text: In means inside. On means on top. Under means below.
examples: The bunny is in the basket.
The cup is on the table.
The ball is under the bed.
rule.say: In means inside. On means on top. Under means below.
sayEx: The bunny is in the basket.
The cup is on the table.
The ball is under the bed.

check.q: The ball is inside the box. The ball is ___ the box.

notes.on: On means on top. Inside is in.
notes.under: Under means below. Inside is in.

check.explain: Inside something is in: in the box.
check.say: The ball is inside the box. The ball is blank the box.

notes.under: Under means below. On top is on.

check.explain: On top of something is on: on the bed.
check.say: The cat is sitting on top of the bed. The cat is blank the bed.

notes.on: On means on top. Below is under.
notes.in: In means inside. Below is under.

check.say: The shoes are below the chair. The shoes are blank the chair.

discover.hint: In is inside the toy box. On is on top of the bed. Under is below the bed.

notes.under: Under means below. The fish is inside the water: in.

check2.explain: Inside the water: in the water.
check2.say: The fish swims inside the water. The fish is blank the water.

check2.q: My hat is on top of my head. My hat is ___ my head.

notes.in: In means inside. A hat sits on top: on.
notes.under: Under means below. A hat sits on top: on.

check2.say: My hat is on top of my head. My hat is blank my head.

notes.in: In means inside. Below is under.

check2.explain: Below the table: under the table.
check2.say: The dog is hiding below the table. The dog is blank the table.

lessons.title: Who? Where? What?
lessons.art_alt: Hoot the owl opens a letter full of question bubbles

hook.text: Hoot found a story letter, but all the answers fell out and got mixed up! The question words can tell us what kind of answer to look for.
hook.say: Hoot found a story letter, but all the answers fell out and got mixed up! The question words can tell us what kind of answer to look for.

discover.text: Drag each answer to the question it fits: Who, Where or What?
discover.hint: Who is a person or an animal. Where is a place. What is a thing.

items.why: Mrs Lee is a person, so she answers Who?
In the park is a place, so it answers Where?
A red ball is a thing, so it answers What?
My grandma is a person: Who?
At school is a place: Where?
A cake is a thing: What?
Under the tree is a place: Where?
Puffbun is an animal friend: Who?

discover.say: Drag each answer to the question it fits: Who, Where or What?

rule.text: Who asks about a person or an animal. Where asks about a place. What asks about a thing. Find the question word first, then look for that kind of answer in the story!
examples: Who is at the door? Grandma.
Where is the cat? On the bed.
What is in the bag? A book.
rule.say: Who asks about a person or an animal. Where asks about a place. What asks about a thing. Find the question word first, then look for that kind of answer in the story!
sayEx: Who is at the door? Grandma.
Where is the cat? On the bed.
What is in the bag? A book.

check.text: Mia has a kite. She flies it in the park with her dad.
check.q: Where does Mia fly the kite?

notes.her dad: Her dad is a person. That answers Who?, not Where?
notes.a kite: A kite is a thing. That answers What?, not Where?

check.explain: Where asks for a place. The story says: in the park.
check.say: Mia has a kite. She flies it in the park with her dad. Where does Mia fly the kite?

check.text: Mia has a kite. She flies it in the park with her dad.
check.q: Who flies the kite with Mia?

notes.in the park: In the park is a place. That answers Where?, not Who?
notes.a kite: A kite is a thing. That answers What?, not Who?

check.explain: Who asks for a person. The story says: with her dad.
check.say: Mia has a kite. She flies it in the park with her dad. Who flies the kite with Mia?

check.text: Mia has a kite. She flies it in the park with her dad.

notes.in the park: In the park is a place. That answers Where?
notes.her dad: Her dad is a person. That answers Who?

check.explain: What asks for a thing. The story says: Mia has a kite.
check.say: Mia has a kite. She flies it in the park with her dad. What does Mia have?

reteach.text: Here's another way. Each question word is a treasure map! Who points to people and animals. Where points to places, and place answers often start with in, on, at or under. What points to things.

discover.text: Follow the treasure map! Drag each answer to its question.
discover.hint: Does it start with in, on or at? Then it's a place: Where?

items.why: Grandpa is a person: Who?
On the bus starts with on, a place: Where?
A sandwich is a thing: What?
At home starts with at, a place: Where?

discover.say: Follow the treasure map! Drag each answer to its question.

reteach.say: Here's another way. Each question word is a treasure map! Who points to people and animals. Where points to places, and place answers often start with in, on, at or under. What points to things.

notes.popcorn: Popcorn is a thing. That answers What?

check2.say: Sam and his cat sit on the sofa. They eat popcorn. Who sits with Sam?

check2.text: Sam and his cat sit on the sofa. They eat popcorn.

notes.his cat: His cat is an animal. That answers Who?
notes.popcorn: Popcorn is a thing. That answers What?

check2.explain: Where asks for a place: on the sofa.
check2.say: Sam and his cat sit on the sofa. They eat popcorn. Where do they sit?

check2.text: Sam and his cat sit on the sofa. They eat popcorn.

notes.his cat: His cat is an animal. That answers Who?

lessons.grown: 👪 Wh- question words (Pre-A1 Starters) as a reading strategy: identify the question word, then scan for that type of answer (person / place / thing).

lessons.title: have / has
lessons.art_alt: Crumb the baker dragon sorts picnic baskets for friends

hook.text: Picnic day! Crumb packed baskets for everyone, but the little words have and has got mixed up on the labels. Can you sort them?
hook.say: Picnic day! Crumb packed baskets for everyone, but the little words have and has got mixed up on the labels. Can you sort them?

discover.text: Who needs have, and who needs has? Drag each friend into the right basket.
discover.hint: I, you, we and they take have. He, she and it take has.

items.why: With I we say have: I have a bun.
She is one girl, so we say has: She has a cake.
They is more than one: They have apples.
He is one boy: He has a pie.
We takes have: We have cookies.
It is one thing: It has a cherry.
You takes have: You have a drink.
My cat is like it: My cat has a ball.

discover.say: Who needs have, and who needs has? Drag each friend into the right basket.

rule.text: I, you, we and they go with have. He, she and it go with has.
examples: I have a bun. We have cookies.
She has a cake. It has a cherry.
rule.say: I, you, we and they go with have. He, she and it go with has.
sayEx: I have a bun. We have cookies.
She has a cake. It has a cherry.

notes.have: Tom is one boy, like he, so we say has.
notes.am: Am goes with I for names and feelings, not for things you own.

check.explain: Tom is like he, so: Tom has a red bike.
check.say: Tom blank a red bike.

notes.has: With I we say have, not has.
notes.is: Is is for am/is/are. Here we need have for owning.

check.explain: I always takes have: I have two sisters.
check.say: I blank two sisters.

check.explain: They goes with have: They have hats.
check.say: Which is right?

reteach.text: Here's another way. Swap the name for a little word first! Mia becomes she, so it's has. Mia and Tom become they, so it's have. Me becomes I, so it's have.
examples: Mia → she → Mia has a kite.
Mia and Tom → they → They have a kite.
me → I → I have a kite.

discover.text: Swap and sort! Drag each one to have or has.
discover.hint: Swap for I, he, she, it, we, you or they first.

items.why: I takes have.
The dog is like it: has.
We takes have.
Lily is like she: has.
You takes have.
Puffbun is one friend, like he/it: has.

discover.say: Swap and sort! Drag each one to have or has.

reteach.say: Here's another way. Swap the name for a little word first! Mia becomes she, so it's has. Mia and Tom become they, so it's have. Me becomes I, so it's have.

notes.has: My friends are more than one, like they, so we say have.
notes.is: Is is for am/is/are. Owning needs have.

check2.explain: Friends are like they: My friends have a ball.

notes.are: Are is for you/we/they with am/is/are.

check2.explain: She takes has: She has a blue bag.

lessons.title: can / can't
lessons.art_alt: Puffbun tries to fly while Hoot watches kindly

hook.text: Puffbun wants to help at Sports Day! Some things Puffbun can do, and some things Puffbun can't. The little word after can stays plain — no -s!
hook.say: Puffbun wants to help at Sports Day! Some things Puffbun can do, and some things Puffbun can't. The little word after can stays plain — no -s!

discover.text: Drag can or can't into each gap. You can also tap a word.
discover.hint: Can = yes, I am able. Can't = no, I am not able. After can/can't the verb stays plain: can jump, not can jumps.

items.why: Fish are able to swim: Fish can swim.
Bunnies are not able to fly: Puffbun can't fly.
You are able to hop: I can hop.
A rock is not able to sing: A rock can't sing.
Birds are able to sing: Birds can sing.
Lily is not a fish: Lily can't breathe under water.

discover.say: Drag can or can't into each gap. You can also tap a word.

rule.text: Can means you are able to do it. Can't means you are not able. After can or can't, keep the verb plain: can swim, can't fly — no -s, no -ed, no -ing.
rule.say: Can means you are able to do it. Can't means you are not able. After can or can't, keep the verb plain: can swim, can't fly — no -s, no -ed, no -ing.

notes.cans: Can does not take -s. Say can fly.

check.say: Birds blank fly.

notes.can: You are not able to touch the moon, so can't.
notes.cans: Can does not take -s. Here we need can't.

check.explain: Nobody can touch the moon from here: I can't touch the moon.
check.say: I blank touch the moon.

After can the verb stays plain: jump, not jumps.
Can never takes -s. Say She can jump.

check.explain: After can, keep the verb plain: She can jump.
check.say: Which is right?

reteach.text: Here's another way. Think of a green light and a red light! Can is the green light: go ahead, you are able. Can't is the red light: stop, you are not able. The action word after the light stays plain.

discover.text: Green light or red light? Drag can or can't.
discover.hint: Able = can. Not able = can't. Verb stays plain.

items.why: Cats are able to climb.

discover.say: Green light or red light? Drag can or can't.

reteach.say: Here's another way. Think of a green light and a red light! Can is the green light: go ahead, you are able. Can't is the red light: stop, you are not able. The action word after the light stays plain.

notes.can to: After can we do not say to. Say can jump.

check2.explain: Frogs are able: Frogs can jump.

After can, use the plain verb: swim, not swimming.

check2.explain: Plain verb after can: He can swim.

lessons.grown: 👪 Modal can / can't for ability (Pre-A1 Starters); bare infinitive after the modal.

lessons.title: he plays, I play
lessons.art_alt: Lily and friends play ball while Sumi stamps a letter s

hook.text: Sports Day verbs! Sumi noticed something funny: I play, you play, we play… but he playS and she playS. A little s sneaks onto the verb for he, she and it!
hook.say: Sports Day verbs! Sumi noticed something funny: I play, you play, we play… but he playS and she playS. A little s sneaks onto the verb for he, she and it!

discover.text: Drag the s stamp onto the verbs that need it. You can also tap a word.
discover.hint: He, she or it before the verb? Stamp s! I, you, we or they? No s.

items.why: He needs s: He plays.
I takes no s: I run.
She needs s: She jumps.
They take no s: They sing.
It needs s: It rains.
We take no s: We read.

discover.say: Drag the s stamp onto the verbs that need it. You can also tap a word.

rule.text: With he, she and it, add s to the verb: he plays, she jumps, it rains. With I, you, we and they, keep the verb plain: I play, they sing.
rule.say: With he, she and it, add s to the verb: he plays, she jumps, it rains. With I, you, we and they, keep the verb plain: I play, they sing.

notes.running: Running is for is + -ing. Here we need runs.
